notes: A selected compilation of six captured CWE pages, 29 named CAPEC patterns and 30 direct taxonomy mappings, plus one publisher-attributed actor/campaign context. It is not a full catalogue or incident census.
Official taxonomy associations are not observed exploitation, actor participation, per-CVE applicability or evidence of an installed environment. CNA-provided weakness membership remains separate.

CAPEC names are supplied by the CWE Related Attack Patterns tables. Six selected CAPEC definition pages were separately captured and qualified as CAPEC 3.9; the other 23 named patterns have no qualified definition page in this compilation.
CWE-287 lists ten patterns; the first eight in source order are retained. CAPEC-650 and CAPEC-94 are omitted by that declared subset limit.
The captured CWE-416 page lacks a Related Attack Patterns section. Its definition is included; no direct mapping is asserted and no global absence is claimed.
CWE evidence versions and modification dates describe the captured CWE pages, not CAPEC releases, incident dates or HTTP capture time.
The Microsoft actor, product and mitigation context is attributed to the captured article. It is not independent identity verification, incident forensics or a current publisher-state observation.
The campaign label is a local descriptive grouping. Empty aliases do not establish global absence. Mitigation statements retain confirmed-suspicion and authorized-response conditions.
Publication, event, source modification, capture and compilation/review clocks remain distinct. Unknown source dates remain null; current retrospective context is not historical as-of proof.
The local catalog version identifies this compilation. It grants no account, device, runtime, remediation or publication permission.
